title: Isotope-Exchange Dynamics in Isostructural Decametalates with Profound Differences in Reactivity
main_article_access_note: No main-article bytes are included or used. Parent acquisition reported publisher 403 and OSTI retrieval timeout; these are access limitations, not scientific evidence.
selection_reason: Site-resolved isotope measurements explicitly separate oxygen signal exchange from molecular transformation; directly relevant to the limits of using oxygen labels to infer oxide-core renewal.

extracted_table.log_convention: Table labels log(k) s^-1 without explicitly defining its base. Reported log differences are primary; CSV log_base=10 is a declared conventional arithmetic assumption, and fold ratios are conditional on it.
extracted_table.site_A_endpoint: rate of transformation of dititanoniobate into a new molecule
extracted_table.other_sites_endpoint: oxygen isotope signal exchange; acidic transformation can also affect signals
extracted_table.missing_values: Blank numeric cells preserve source --. Three acidic Site D entries are too fast to estimate with no numeric bound; all other -- entries remain not_reported.
extracted_table.rate_uncertainty: error of regression or standard deviation of repeated trials, whichever is larger; no confidence level supplied

qualitative_source_locations.S2_Table_S-1-1: Buffers and 0.1 M tetramethylammonium chloride background electrolyte
qualitative_source_locations.S4_Figure_S-1-1: pH 8.49, 35.5 C: D/F/G oxygen signals essentially gone after 3 hours
qualitative_source_locations.S5_Figure_S-1-2: pH 8.03, 35.5 C: C/E decline over several weeks while A/B remain constant; authors interpret no molecular transformation
qualitative_source_locations.S8_Figure_S-1-5: D too fast below pH 8.0 at 35.5 C; lowering to 6.0 C permits estimates
